To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the landscape of Hitec city is characterized by the presence of a number of actors, who are differently prioritized and differently represented in the space.

the spatial form of the landscape of Hitec city in Hyderabad, India is a result of the grobalization process, which involves the imposition of a global image, the global-as-spectacle on the space, which is achieved through the stratification of the space and exclusion of certain actors, the non-persons.
Hitec City is a layered space where global flows, particularly the process of grobailization, is evident in the form of exclusion and stratification of the landscape.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the ways in which globalization is spatially manifested, and how it produces certain forms of stratification.
understanding the ways in which the global non-person is rendered as invisible as necessary, in the context where the grobal-as- spectacle is prioritized.

the following: (1) the spatialization of globalization, and its impact on the production of space, particularly in the form of layered spaces; (2) the role played by the built form and the built landscape in the production of space and in the process of globalization; and (3) the role played in this process by the spatial practices of the global non-person.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the landscape in Hitec City is not merely a reflection of globalization, but is also an active participant in the production of globalization, and the grobal-as- spectacle.
globalization, and grobalization in particular, is an important factor in creating and maintaining the layered space that is Hitec City.
globalization is not just about flows and connections; it is about stratification and polarization as well.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Hitec City is a grobalized space, where the global is projected as a spectacle, and the local is marginalized and rendered invisible.
globalization and grobalization, in the context in which they are being discussed, are not only about flows of people and capital.
globalization is not a uniform process, but a complex one that involves the interplay of various actors and processes at different scales.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the grobalization of the space in Hitec City is not just a matter of the physical form, but is also related to a process of erasure, where the global non-person is rendered invisible through the physical form, as well as through the media, in order to maintain the global-as-spectacle.

the process of globalization, particularly the process of gro-balization, is a process that is not just about the flow of people and ideas, but also about the flow of power and the imposition of a particular global image, which in the case of India is the image of an emerging global city.

the process of globalization and the process of grobali-zation are not the same, and that grobalization, as an imperialistic imposition of a particular global image on a space, may be seen as an important aspect of contemporary globalization.
